skill.name: routeros-command-tree
skill.description: Guides RouterOS command tree introspection with the /console/inspect REST API for schema generation and command mapping.
skill.summary: Map RouterOS command trees and convert inspect data into API schemas.
skill.author: tikoci

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, code fences, RouterOS path examples, and local documentation links. The real concern is operational: live /console/inspect traversal can issue many RouterOS REST requests, and the skill documents syntax lookups that can crash the RouterOS HTTP server unless skipped. No prompt injection or data exfiltration intent was found.

remediation.suggestion: Keep the dangerous path skip list in generated tooling and test syntax lookups with cached inspect data before using a live router.
Add rate limits, timeouts, and explicit user confirmation before full live tree traversal because it can send many requests.
Require credentials through approved secret storage and avoid printing authorization headers or sensitive router responses.

content.value_statement: RouterOS command trees are hard to inspect and convert into schemas. This skill explains /console/inspect traversal, REST verb mapping, and safe schema generation.
actual_capabilities: Explains RouterOS command tree node types and path formats.
Shows how /rest/console/inspect child and syntax requests work.
Describes recursive traversal patterns and dangerous path skips.
Maps RouterOS CLI commands to REST verbs for schema generation.
Explains inspect.json, RAML, and OpenAPI output formats.
limitations: Does not provide executable scripts or RouterOS credentials.
Requires RouterOS 7.x or a cached inspect.json file for real data.
Full live traversal can be slow and send many HTTP requests.
Command trees vary by RouterOS version and installed packages.

use_cases.title: Generate RouterOS API Schemas
use_cases.description: Convert inspected command paths into RAML or OpenAPI models for internal tooling.

use_cases.title: Understand RouterOS REST Mapping
use_cases.description: Map CLI commands such as add, set, remove, and print to the correct REST verbs.

use_cases.title: Review Command Tree Coverage
use_cases.description: Compare inspect.json files across RouterOS versions to document command and package differences.

prompt_templates.title: Explain the Command Tree
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner overview of RouterOS inspect concepts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain how the RouterOS command tree is structured. Include dir, path, cmd, and arg node types.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Inspect Traversal
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a safe traversal approach for a live router.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me plan a RouterOS /console/inspect traversal. Include request types, path format, rate limits, and dangerous path skips.

prompt_templates.title: Map Commands to REST
prompt_templates.scenario: Translate CLI behavior into REST schema methods.
prompt_templates.prompt: Map RouterOS CLI commands to REST verbs for schema generation. Explain add, set, remove, get, print, and other commands.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Schema Generator
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture for generated API documentation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a RouterOS inspect.json to OpenAPI generator. Include traversal inputs, command mapping, argument handling, caching, and safety checks.

output_examples.output: The skill explains that inspect paths use comma-separated segments. It contrasts root, single path, command, and argument paths.

output_examples.input: Summarize safe traversal rules for a live router.
output_examples.output: The response lists child enumeration, syntax lookup rules, dangerous path skips, caching with inspect.json, and live request limits.

output_examples.input: Describe how RouterOS commands become REST methods.
output_examples.output: The response maps create, update, delete, list, single read, and action commands to their RouterOS REST method patterns.

best_practices: Use cached inspect.json data during development whenever possible.
Skip syntax lookups for documented dangerous path segments.
Confirm RouterOS version and installed packages before comparing schemas.
anti_patterns: Do not run full live traversal without timeouts and rate limits.
Do not assume standard REST semantics for RouterOS create and update operations.
Do not reuse inspect data across RouterOS versions without validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps explain and use RouterOS /console/inspect data for command lookup and API schema generation.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, examples, mappings, and safety notes for building your own tooling.

faq.question: Which RouterOS versions are covered?
faq.answer: The skill describes RouterOS 7.x behavior. Actual command trees depend on version and installed packages.

faq.question: Can it generate OpenAPI directly?
faq.answer: It explains the data model and mappings needed for generation, but it does not ship a generator.

faq.question: Why are some syntax lookups skipped?
faq.answer: The skill states that specific RouterOS scripting paths can crash the REST server when queried for argument syntax.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
